key_decisions: One movement type per file, always. The S08 two-step tilt (sh076) is encoded as a single tilt_up with a two_step speed curve, not as two moves; sh053's ride is a single vertical follow with a tiny (about 0.10 m) amplitude and no second axis.

Every move is grounded in its own shot's duration: no moving shot is under 3.0 s, and each file states a rate (m/s or degrees) that fits the shot length. The 0.5-2.5 s shots (sh020, sh023, sh072, sh075, sh077, sh085, sh100, sh101) are all locked frames.

The three hold-for-the-whole-shot takes (sh025 9.0 s, sh048 12.0 s, sh086-sh087) are static with no move available at all: sh048's twelve unmoving seconds are what make the shrink read as forced perspective instead of an edit or an effect.

Lens, height and angle are instances of cinematography.json's focal_rules and scale_lens_map, not new choices. The two rationed 24 mm shots and the single 100 mm are spent on exactly the three images that file names.

The giant-state ceiling is enforced from sh068 onward: no lens above 1.00 m for the rest of the episode. The only set-up near the lamp line is sh064, which cinematography.json explicitly licenses as the last one allowed there. sh076's tilt runs out of room against her own bulk, so no lamp fixture can enter frame.
S10 never leaves the water: every lens is 0.05-0.20 m and the one travelling shot (sh099) stays on the surface - no crane, drone or high view anywhere.
Focus is never pulled anywhere in the episode (dof_policy budget of zero), so rack_focus is 'none' in all 101 files.

constraints_that_forced_my_hand.constraint: 'Locked - no camera move' / 'the frame DOES NOT MOVE for twelve seconds' / 'read off the set, not the lens'
constraints_that_forced_my_hand.effect: Static was the only legal answer; the size change and the fall are carried entirely by the set travelling or substituting inside a fixed frame.

constraints_that_forced_my_hand.effect: No pan with the rabbit, and no focus emphasis - the camera refuses to acknowledge him.

constraints_that_forced_my_hand.effect: Two shots that ask to be follows are locked instead; both end on a deliberately emptied frame.

conflicts_found.between: cinematography.json focal_rules.garden… pov_lens_rule ('six of the seven POVs are 40 mm', listing the flooded canyon in S10) vs focal_rules.flooded_canyon_wide (28 mm, and it names 'POV 7 of 7')

conflicts_found.item: sh075 is shot on 40 mm, not the 28 mm the giant_fragment rule would default to.
conflicts_found.why: The frame is her hand and the lower half of her face coming into the top of a water-level close. A 28 mm that near a face risks the facial distortion style.json bans (CR-001), and the shot is the reverse of sh073/sh074 on the same water-level eyeline, where 40 mm is the established lens.
conflicts_found.route_to: 07-directing/cinematography for acknowledgement; recorded in the shot's own movement_note.

deviations.item: The static/moving ratio comes out at about 87/13 by shot count (85/15 by screen time), not the directing plan's 'about 70/30'.
deviations.why: The same section of the plan enumerates the licensed moves - following her walk or run, the single S05 hall reveal, and the S08 failed tilt - and the frozen shot_list then pins most remaining shots with an explicit constraint ('Static', 'Locked - no camera move', 'no pan, no reframe', 'the camera does NOT follow her down', 'not by a push-in'). Honouring the enumeration and the per-shot constraints leaves thirteen moves. Reaching 30 % would require inventing moves the plan does not license and several constraints forbid outright.
deviations.decided: Resolved in favour of the explicit licence list and the locked constraints. Every licensed move is taken, plus the four camera-height follows the shot_list's own camera_position fields specify (sh013, sh026, sh039, sh053) and the swim in sh099.
deviations.route_to: orchestrator -> 07-directing/director, for disclosure only. If the director wants the ratio nearer 70/30, the candidates are sh030, sh032, sh051, sh066 and sh090 (all currently static by choice rather than by constraint); that is a plan change, not a rework I will make on my own.

deviations.item: sh053's 'riding up a little with each attempt and dropping back with her' is delivered as one low-amplitude vertical follow (about 0.10 m, three beats), not as three separate camera events.
deviations.why: One camera move per shot is the model's hard guidance; an oscillating or compound move on a nine-second shot is the classic source of unstable generation.
deviations.decided: Single movement token pedestal_follow, single axis, amplitude kept small enough to read as the camera staying with her body rather than as a camera performance.

machine_checks.check: movement_supported + one_move_per_shot + schema + shot_list agreement + lens budgets + post-sh068 height ceiling + zero rack focus
machine_checks.detail: 101/101 files present and valid JSON; every movement is a single token from the supported vocabulary with no compound or contradictory value; shot_id, group_id, duration_s and size agree with shot_list for all 101; no move in a shot under 3.0 s; no moving shot against a constraint that forbids movement; lens values all inside the 24/28/40/50/100 set with the 24 mm budget at 2/2 and the 100 mm at 1/1; no lens above 1.00 m from sh068 onward; rack_focus 'none' on all 101.

acceptance_self_run.movement_supported: PASS - every movement is a standard camera term the video model executes directly, single-move per shot, and each is consistent with its shot's size, duration and constraint field.

acceptance_self_run.qa: not run - all QA dimensions are 0

skills.reason: Performance-control skill is owned by blocking (intent layer) and prompt (evidence layer); this station designs camera movement only and produces no performance layer. No skill is auto-activated for 07-directing/camera-movement.

handoff.08-video-gen/prompt: Each camera.json carries exactly one movement term plus its direction, speed and easing - quote the movement as a single camera instruction per shot and do not combine it with any other move. 88 shots are static: write them as a fixed frame and let the described subject or set motion carry the shot. Lens values are 35 mm-equivalent and are to be written verbatim ('shot on a 40 mm lens'). Nothing in these files licenses a zoom, a rack focus or a transition.
handoff.08-video-gen/video-generation: No move depends on a previous group's tail frame; every group's camera starts fresh (long_take off). The thirteen moving shots are listed above - if any of them re-rolls badly, the fallback is the same set-up held static, not a different move.
handoff.07-directing/composition: Start and end framings in each file name the gauges that must be in frame (bottle / dado / flag joint / tabletop / lamp line / vault rib / door leaf / waterline). At every size beat both gauges are inside the frame and deep focus, per dof_policy.
handoff.07-directing/blocking: Four shots hand the camera's height to her body rather than the reverse: sh013, sh026, sh039 (the lens drops or rises with her) and sh078-sh082, where a 0.55-0.60 m lens reaches her face only because the pose is hunched and folded. The travelling shots sh034, sh038, sh058, sh059, sh089 and sh099 assume constant pace - no stops inside the move.
handoff.07-directing/continuity-planning: Movement-direction continuity to check: sh034 (south along the west doors) vs sh038 (the same axis reversed); sh058 out vs sh059 back on one axis; sh089 repeats sh034's axis at a third of the height; sh093 exits bottom-left and sh094 surfaces bottom-left to match; sh099 heads south toward the brightest water and sh100/sh101 hold that same axis.

not_done_and_why: No capability list was attached to the work order, so the supported-movement whitelist above was derived from the project's video model and its prompt-engineering guide rather than from a supplied document. If the scheduler has a formal list, it should be checked against the eight movement tokens used here - all eight are standard terms and none is exotic.
The static/moving ratio was not forced up to the plan's 70/30 (see DEV-CAM-1); routed to the director rather than worked around.
Group-level camera continuity beyond adjacent-shot direction is continuity-planning's to aggregate; I have listed the pairs that matter in the handoff.
